guide: Service is using what we can do to help other people, without being asked and without expecting a reward. In a classroom it shows up when children notice a need and do something about it.
Compassion is noticing how someone else feels and wanting to help them feel better. It starts with paying attention to faces, words and actions.

meaning: Noticing what others do for us
guide: Gratitude is noticing the people and things that help us and saying thank you. It turns what we take for granted into something we appreciate.
Justice means treating people fairly, so everyone gets a fair turn, a fair share and a fair rule. Children learn it by seeing what happens when the rules are not the same for everyone.
Perseverance is keeping going when something is hard, by trying again, changing the plan or asking for help. Mistakes become information instead of a reason to quit.
Curiosity is wanting to find out how things work and asking what if. It leads children to try things, look closely and ask good questions.
Teamwork is working with others toward a shared goal, which means listening, sharing jobs and fitting your part with theirs. The result is something no one could make alone.
Honesty is telling the truth about what we did and what we found, even when it is not flattering. It builds the trust that lets people rely on each other's work.
